title: Car insurance renewal
text:
The car insurance with Harbourline expires on 14 November. The renewal quote came in at 612 pounds, up from 540 last year, mostly because of the new postcode band.

Comparison sites show two cheaper options with the same excess and windscreen cover. Ask Harbourline to match before switching; they matched last year after one phone call.

Remember to add the no-claims certificate and the dashcam discount code when filling in the new application.

title: Car service log
text:
Oil change and new air filter at Dunmore Garage in March, 48,200 miles. The mechanic said the front brake pads have about 3 mm left.

Replaced front brake pads and discs in July at 51,900 miles. Total 286 pounds including labour. Tyres rotated at the same visit.

Next MOT is due in February. The rear wiper blade squeaks and should be replaced before then.

title: Home EV charger installation
text:
Three installers quoted for a 7 kW wallbox on the driveway. Voltwise was cheapest at 899 pounds but needs a new isolator switch fitted first.

The charger needs a dedicated circuit from the consumer unit and an earth rod outside. The electrician can do both on the same day.

Check whether the off-peak electricity tariff requires a smart charger with scheduling before choosing a model.

title: Boiler breakdown and repair
text:
The boiler stopped firing on Sunday night; the display showed fault code F28, which means ignition failure. No hot water or radiators until the engineer came.

The heating engineer replaced the gas valve and the ignition electrode on Tuesday. The call-out and parts came to 240 pounds, covered partly by the home emergency plan.

The engineer recommended a power flush next autumn because the radiators upstairs are cold at the top.

title: Roof leak in the spare bedroom
text:
Water stain spreading on the spare bedroom ceiling after the storm. The drip only appears during heavy rain from the west.

The roofer found two slipped slates and cracked flashing around the chimney. He replaced the slates and resealed the flashing for 380 pounds.

Repaint the ceiling with stain-block primer once it has dried out completely, probably in a month.

title: Kitchen renovation quotes
text:
Three builders quoted for the kitchen renovation. Oakline estimate 18,500 pounds including worktops; Brightwell estimate 16,900 without appliances.

Brightwell can start in April and expects four weeks of work. Oakline is booked until June but includes the electrical certificate.

Decide on quartz versus laminate worktops before asking for revised estimates. The island needs two extra sockets.

title: Spring garden planting plan
text:
Raised bed one: tomatoes, basil and marigolds. Raised bed two: courgettes and runner beans along the fence.

Sow sweet peas indoors in February and plant them out after the last frost, usually mid April here.

The apple tree needs pruning in winter while it is dormant. Mulch the roses with compost in March.

title: Home insurance policy
text:
Buildings and contents insurance is with Clearwater Mutual, renewing on 2 March. Accidental damage cover was added this year.

The policy excludes damage from gradual leaks, so the roof repair was not claimable. Valuables over 1,500 pounds must be listed individually.

Bikes are covered away from home up to 800 pounds each.

title: Dental check-up and hygienist
text:
Six-monthly check-up at Riverside Dental on 9 October at 14:20. The hygienist appointment follows straight after.

Last visit the dentist noted a small cavity on a lower molar and suggested a filling if it grows. Use the softer toothbrush and floss nightly.

title: Physiotherapy for knee pain
text:
The physiotherapist thinks the knee pain is patellofemoral syndrome from increasing running mileage too fast.

Exercises: clamshells, single-leg squats to a chair, and foam rolling the outer thigh. Three sets of twelve, every other day.

Review appointment in four weeks. Keep runs under 30 minutes and avoid downhill sections until then.

title: Flu vaccination reminder
text:
The pharmacy on Mill Street is offering the seasonal flu vaccine from 1 October. Book online; walk-ins only on Saturdays.

Dad is eligible for the free jab through the surgery because he is over 65. Book his and mine for the same morning.

title: Blood test results
text:
The annual blood test came back mostly normal. Cholesterol is 5.4, slightly above the target, and vitamin D was low at the end of winter.

The doctor suggested a vitamin D supplement from October to March and another cholesterol check in six months. Less cheese, more oats.

title: Repeat prescription
text:
The repeat prescription for the antihistamine and the inhaler is due on the 3rd of each month. Request it through the surgery app five days before.

The pharmacy delivers on Thursdays if the order is ready by Tuesday afternoon.

title: Self assessment tax return
text:
The self assessment for the last tax year is due online by 31 January. Rental income from the flat and the freelance invoices both need to go on it.

Deductible expenses: letting agent fees, the boiler service at the flat, and a share of the home office broadband.

Pay the balancing payment and the first payment on account together. Keep receipts for five years.

title: Remortgage options
text:
The fixed rate on the mortgage ends in May. The lender's product transfer offers 4.6 percent for five years with no fee.

A broker found 4.3 percent with a 999 pound arrangement fee at another bank. Over five years the broker deal saves roughly 1,400 pounds after fees.

Need the latest payslips, a valuation and three months of bank statements for the switch.

title: Monthly household budget
text:
Household budget. Fixed costs each month: mortgage 1,120, council tax 168, energy 142, broadband 32, phones 28, insurance 61.

Groceries average 520 a month; eating out crept up to 190 in the summer. Target is 120.

Move 300 a month into the holiday pot and 200 into the emergency fund on payday.

title: Pension contributions
text:
Workplace pension contributions are 5 percent from salary plus 4 percent employer match. Salary sacrifice would save national insurance.

Raise contributions to 8 percent after the pay rise in April. Check the old pension pot from the previous employer and consider consolidating it.

title: Annual salary review
text:
The annual pay review meeting with Priya is on 12 March. Market data suggests backend roles at this level pay 8 to 12 percent more.

Prepare examples: the search latency work, mentoring two new hires, and leading the Kestrel migration. Ask about the senior promotion criteria.

title: Lisbon long weekend itinerary
text:
Friday: arrive at 11:00, check in at the guesthouse in Alfama, tram 28 to Graça, dinner at a tasca near the cathedral.

Saturday: Belém in the morning for the tower and pastéis, LX Factory in the afternoon, sunset at Miradouro de Santa Catarina.

Sunday: day trip to Sintra by train from Rossio. Book Pena Palace tickets for the first time slot to avoid queues.

title: Japan trip planning
text:
Two weeks in Japan in April for the cherry blossom: Tokyo, Kanazawa, Kyoto and Osaka.

The seven-day rail pass only pays off if we do Tokyo to Kanazawa and Kyoto to Hiroshima within the same week. Otherwise buy single tickets.

Book the ryokan in Kyoto early; the one near Gion fills up by January. Get a Suica card on arrival for local trains.

title: Passport renewal
text:
My passport expires next August. Several countries require six months validity on entry, so renew it before the Japan trip.

The online renewal needs a digital photo and the old passport sent by post. Standard processing takes about three weeks.

title: Flight booking confirmation
text:
Booking reference QX7H2P. Outbound flight to Lisbon departs Gatwick at 07:05 on Friday, arriving 09:55 local time.

Return flight departs Lisbon at 18:40 on Sunday. One cabin bag each; seats 14A and 14B. Online check-in opens 24 hours before departure.

title: Packing list for weekend trips
text:
Passport, chargers, travel adapter, toiletries under 100 ml in a clear bag, reusable water bottle, and a light rain jacket.

For city breaks bring comfortable walking shoes and a small day bag. Download offline maps before leaving.

title: Project Kestrel: Postgres migration plan
text:
Kestrel moves the orders service from MySQL to Postgres 16. Phase one runs dual writes behind a feature flag while a backfill copies historical orders.

Phase two switches reads to Postgres for 5 percent of traffic, comparing results with the shadow reader. Phase three cuts over fully once mismatches stay below 0.01 percent for a week.

Owners: Sam for the backfill, Lena for the shadow reader, Omar for the cutover runbook.

title: Kestrel migration standup notes
text:
Kestrel standup: the backfill of historical orders to Postgres is 70 percent done. Dual writes have been on for three days with no errors.

The shadow reader found mismatches in currency rounding for refunds. Lena is fixing the decimal precision in the Postgres schema.

Cutover is still planned for the second week of September if mismatches stay low.

title: Kestrel cutover rollback plan
text:
If error rates rise after the cutover, flip the reads flag back to MySQL first; dual writes keep MySQL current so no data is lost.

If dual writes themselves fail, stop the writer, replay the outbox from the last checkpoint, and reconcile with the nightly diff job.

Rollback decision owner is Omar. Page the database on-call before starting any rollback.

title: Q4 team objectives
text:
Objective one: make search feel instant. Key results: p95 search latency under 150 ms and zero timeouts on the mobile app.

Objective two: finish the Kestrel migration and decommission the MySQL cluster by December.

Objective three: reduce on-call pages by 30 percent by fixing the top five noisy alerts.

title: Hiring a backend engineer
text:
We are hiring a senior backend engineer for the payments team. The interview loop is a phone screen, a systems design session and a pairing exercise.

Three candidates are in the pipeline. Ana's take-home was the strongest; schedule her onsite before the end of the month.

Recruiter contact is Joe at Talentbridge; the agency fee is 18 percent of first-year salary.

title: Postmortem: API outage on 3 June
text:
The public API was down for 47 minutes on 3 June. A config deploy set the connection pool size to zero on all gateway nodes.

Detection took 12 minutes because the health check only tested the process, not database connectivity.

Actions: validate config values in CI, add a synthetic transaction check, and require two reviewers for gateway config changes.

title: On-call runbook
text:
When paged, acknowledge within five minutes and post in the incident channel. Severity one means customer-facing impact.

For gateway errors, check the connection pool dashboard and the last config deploy first. Roll back the deploy if it is less than an hour old.

Hand over open incidents at the Monday rotation with a written summary.

title: Design review: search ranking
text:
Proposal: replace the keyword-only search with hybrid ranking that fuses bm25 with embedding similarity using reciprocal rank fusion.

Open questions from the review: how to evaluate offline, whether to diversify results, and the latency budget for embedding the query.

Decision: build a labelled evaluation set first and report recall at ten before switching the default.

title: School term dates
text:
Autumn term starts on 3 September and half term runs from 27 to 31 October. Term ends on 19 December.

Inset days: 2 September and 5 January. Spring term starts on 6 January.

title: Parents evening notes
text:
Met Mr Hale at parents evening. Maya is doing well in maths and reading but is quiet in group work.

He suggested encouraging her to join the debate club and practising times tables for ten minutes a day.

title: Swimming lessons for the children
text:
Maya and Leo start swimming lessons at the leisure centre on Saturdays at 9:30. Leo is in stage two, Maya in stage four.

Bring goggles and a swim hat. The term costs 96 pounds each, paid by direct debit.

title: Biscuit's vet visit
text:
Took Biscuit to the vet for his annual booster and a check of his ears. The vet found a mild ear infection and prescribed drops for seven days.

His weight is 14.2 kg, slightly up; cut treats and add a second walk. Next booster due in twelve months.

title: Biscuit's food allergy
text:
Biscuit keeps scratching and chewing his paws. The vet suspects a chicken allergy and recommended an elimination diet.

Switch to a single-protein salmon kibble for eight weeks with no other treats, then reintroduce chicken and watch for itching.

title: Sourdough bread method
text:
Feed the starter the night before. Mix 500 g strong flour, 350 g water and 100 g active starter; rest one hour, then add 10 g salt.

Four sets of stretch and folds over two hours, then bulk ferment until risen by half. Shape, then cold proof in the fridge overnight.

Bake in a preheated Dutch oven at 250 degrees for 20 minutes with the lid on and 25 minutes with it off.

title: Weeknight lasagna
text:
Brown 500 g beef mince with onion and garlic, add passata and oregano, simmer 30 minutes.

Make a quick white sauce with butter, flour and milk. Layer sauce, pasta sheets and ragu three times, finish with mozzarella.

Bake at 190 degrees for 40 minutes. Freezes well in portions.

title: Chickpea and spinach curry
text:
Fry onion, ginger and garlic, then add curry paste, a tin of chickpeas and a tin of coconut milk. Simmer 20 minutes.

Stir in two handfuls of spinach at the end and finish with lime juice. Serve with rice or flatbread. Vegan and ready in 30 minutes.

title: Meal plan for the week
text:
Meal plan: Monday chickpea curry, Tuesday lasagna leftovers, Wednesday salmon with greens, Thursday homemade pizza, Friday takeaway.

Shopping list: chickpeas, coconut milk, spinach, salmon fillets, mozzarella, flour, lemons and limes.

title: Notes on async Rust
text:
Holding a std Mutex guard across an await point makes the future not Send and can deadlock under a multi-threaded runtime. Use tokio's Mutex or drop the guard first.

spawn_blocking is for CPU-heavy or blocking work such as synchronous SQLite calls; it runs on a separate thread pool.

Cancellation drops the future at its next await point, so cleanup must not rely on code after an await running.

title: NAS backup strategy
text:
Photos and documents live on the NAS with RAID 1. That protects against a disk failure but not against deletion or ransomware.

Nightly snapshots are kept for 30 days. A weekly encrypted copy goes to cloud storage, and a USB drive is rotated to my parents' house each month.

Test a restore every quarter; last test restored 2,000 photos in 40 minutes.

title: Wi-Fi mesh setup
text:
Installed a three-node mesh: main unit by the router, one on the landing, one in the garden office. Backhaul over ethernet for the office node.

Guest network on a separate SSID with client isolation. Smart plugs and cameras on an IoT network with no access to the NAS.

title: Choosing a new laptop
text:
Shortlist for the new laptop: a 14 inch model with 32 GB RAM for running local models, or a lighter 13 inch with 16 GB and better battery life.

Must have: two USB-C ports, a good keyboard, Linux support. Budget up to 1,800 pounds. Wait for the November sales before buying.

title: Moving to a new password manager
text:
Exported the vault from the old password manager and imported it into the new one. 412 logins came across; passkeys had to be recreated.

Turn on two-factor authentication for the new account, print the recovery kit and store it with the important documents.

Delete the export file securely once the import has been checked.

title: Gift ideas for Mum's birthday
text:
Mum's birthday is on 17 November. Ideas: a pottery class voucher, the new biography she mentioned, or a weekend in the Lake District.

Last year we gave her a scarf and theatre tickets; she loved the theatre. Ask Dad what she has hinted at recently.

title: Tom and Ellie's wedding
text:
RSVP to Tom and Ellie's wedding by 1 August. The ceremony is at 2pm in Ludlow on 19 September, reception at the barn afterwards.

Book the hotel in Ludlow for two nights; the gift list is at the department store online. Dress code is summer formal.

title: Book club notes
text:
This month's book club pick was a novel about a lighthouse keeper. Most people liked the first half more than the ending.

Next month we are reading a history of the printing press. Meeting at Grace's flat on the 14th at 7pm.

title: Marathon training plan
text:
Sixteen-week plan for the spring marathon. Long run on Sundays building from 10 miles to 20 miles, with a cutback week every fourth week.

Tuesday intervals, Thursday tempo run, two easy runs. Strength work twice a week for the knees and hips.

Target pace 5:20 per kilometre. Practise fuelling with gels on every long run over 90 minutes.

title: Cancelling the gym membership
text:
The gym membership has a 30-day notice period and must be cancelled in writing. Sent the email on 2 October, so the last payment is in November.

Keep the confirmation email in case they take another direct debit.

title: Switching energy supplier
text:
The fixed electricity and gas tariff ends in December. The current supplier's new rate would raise the bill by about 20 pounds a month.

An off-peak tariff with cheap overnight electricity suits the EV charger. Submit a meter reading on the switch date.

title: Broadband contract
text:
The broadband contract with Skyline Fibre ends on 30 November. The out-of-contract price jumps from 32 to 48 pounds a month.

A competitor offers 900 Mbps full fibre for 35 pounds on an 18 month contract with free installation.

title: Council tax
text:
Council tax is band D, 2,016 pounds a year paid over ten monthly instalments. Switch to twelve instalments to lower the monthly amount.

Single person discount does not apply. Check whether the garden office affects the valuation band.

title: Car finance agreement
text:
The car finance agreement has 14 monthly payments of 189 pounds left. Settling early saves about 120 pounds of interest.

The settlement figure is valid for 28 days from the date of the letter.

title: Online order returns
text:
The jacket from the online order is too small. The returns policy allows 30 days and the label is in the parcel.

Drop it at the parcel shop and keep the receipt until the refund appears.

title: Fixing the bike
text:
The rear derailleur on the bike skips gears. Replaced the gear cable and adjusted the limit screws; still slipping on the smallest cog.

The bike shop says the chain is stretched and the cassette is worn. New chain and cassette quoted at 85 pounds.

title: Film night list
text:
Films to watch: a Studio Ghibli classic for the children, the new documentary about deep sea exploration, and a noir double bill.

Popcorn maker is in the garage. Friday evenings work best.
